## T1 on platform change

T1_ON_PLATFORM_CHANGE: CANNOT_TELL

T1 makes a failure of N1–N4 at qualification or resume the condition; its changed-science parenthetical states the consequence. The first compared quotation likewise gives the implication from an N-condition failure to the changed branch. Neither implication establishes the converse.

N3 enumerates platform-pin fields, prohibits updates from qualification through the resume deadline, and separately requires exact reproduction of MB r1's committed non-target records. It does not explicitly state whether the qualification platform pin must equal MB r1's original platform pin or may describe the newly qualified platform. N1 requires identical pins among the frozen science artifacts, but the quoted definitions do not explicitly resolve whether those include the original platform-pin values. A changed host or libm alone is not explicitly formulated as a standalone N-condition failure in these quotations.

Thus the quoted definitions do not establish that every change of host, OS, interpreter build or libm necessarily fails an N-condition by construction. They also do not establish that such a change preserves every N-condition. An exact non-target reproduction match alone does not settle that interpretive gap. This is a bounded textual reading; it is not a finding that T1 has remained unfired on any actual host, a new risk rating, or permission to lower a rating.
